grammarPoints.title: I **have watched** Japanese anime twice. Eddy **has never watched** Japanese anime.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けい（経けい験けん用よう法ほう）：これまでに経けい験けんがあることを表あらわすには〈have [has] + 過か去こ分ぶん詞し〉の形かたちを使つかい、これを現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けいという。肯こう定てい文ぶんでは回かい数すうの表ひょう現げんやbeforeを、否ひ定てい文ぶんではneverをよく使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Tense (Experiential Use). It describes experiences that have happened up until the present moment, using the structure ⟨have [has] + Past Participle⟩. Frequency expressions (like twice) are common in affirmative sentences, and never is common in negative sentences.
examples: I **have visited** an anime event five times.
Anna **has read** a lot of manga until today.

grammarPoints.title: Have you **ever been** to an anime event? —Yes, I have. [No, I have not. I have **never been** to one.]
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けいの疑ぎ問もん文ぶん: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けいの疑ぎ問もん文ぶんではhave [has]が主しゅ語ごの前まえに出でる。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんではeverをよく使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Tense in interrogative form. In questions, have [or has] precedes the subject. The word ever is frequently used in questions concerning experience.
examples: **Have** you **ever bought** a Japanese manga? —Yes, I have. [No, I haven’t. I’ve **never bought** one.]
**Have** you **ever joined** an anime event? —Yes, I have. [No, I haven’t. I’ve **never joined** one.]

grammarPoints.title: Anime songs **make** me **happy**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: make + （代だい）名めい詞し + 形けい容よう詞し: 「…（名めい詞し）を ～（形けい容よう詞し）の状じょう態たいにする」という意味いみになる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This uses the structure 'make + (pronoun/noun) + adjective' (SVOC), meaning 'to cause... (the noun) to become ~ (the adjective) state'.
examples: Playing video games **makes** us **excited**.
Listening to anime songs **makes** me **very happy**.

grammarPoints.title: The story **shows** me **that** anything is possible.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: SVOO（that節せつ）: 「（人ひと）に（～ということ）を…する」という意味いみになる。前まえの動どう詞しは、show、tell、teachなどがよく使つかわれる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the SVOO structure using a that-clause as the second object. It means 'to do... (the action) (to the person) (the fact/idea)'. Verbs such as show, tell, and teach are commonly used.
examples: The story **teaches** me **that** doing my best is important.
The anime **shows** us **that** efforts will pay off.

grammarPoints.title: Higashiyama **sounds** nice, but I really **want** to visit Kinkaku-ji Temple.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: Real Life English (Discussion): 話はなしの流ながれを示しめす語ご (but, so) を使つかい、逆ぎゃくの意い見けんや結けつ論ろんを導どう入にゅうする。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Used for stating a contrasting preference or opinion after acknowledging a previous point. (The sentence uses 'sounds' followed by an adjective and 'but' to introduce a preference.)
examples: N/A
N/A

grammarPoints.title: I **have just finished** my homework. **Have** you **finished** your homework **yet**? —Yes, I have. I **have already finished** it.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けい（完了よう法ほう）： 「…したところです」という意味いみ。肯こう定てい文ぶんではjustやalready、疑ぎ問もん文ぶん・否ひ定てい文ぶんではyetをよく使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Tense (Completion Use), meaning 'have just finished...' or that an action has been completed. Just and already are often used in affirmative sentences, while yet is used in questions and negative sentences.
examples: **Have** you **cleaned** your room **yet**? —Yes, I have. [No, I haven’t. I **haven’t cleaned** it **yet**.]
**Have** you **washed** your shoes **yet**? —Yes, I have. [No, I haven’t. I **haven’t washed** them **yet**.]

grammarPoints.title: I **have lived** in Japan **for** five years. How long **have** you **lived** in Japan? —**For** five years.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう形けい（継けい続ぞく用よう法ほう）：過か去このある時ときにから現げん在ざいまで、ある状じょう態たいが続つづいていることを表あらわす。あとにはfor ...やsince ...をよく使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Tense (Continuity Use), describing a state or action that began in the past and continues up to the present. It is often followed by for... (duration) or since... (starting point).
examples: I **have had** a dog **for four years**.
I **have been** a big fan of judo **since** I first watched it.

grammarPoints.title: I **have been reading** a book **since** 4 p.m.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう進しん行こう形けい: 〈have [has] + been + ...ing〉の形かたちで、過か去このある時ときから現げん在ざいまで、ある動どう作さが続つづいていることを表あらわす。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Progressive Tense, using the structure ⟨have [has] + been + -ing⟩. It describes an action that started in the past and has been continuously ongoing until the present moment.
examples: Mr. Tani **has been checking** his students’ homework **since 4 p.m**.
It **has been raining** **for two days**.

grammarPoints.title: Actually, more than five million tons of food **is wasted** there every year.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: Real Life English (Lecture): 受うけ身みを使つかった表ひょう現げんで確かく認にんしましょう。（受うけ身み）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This sentence uses the passive voice to highlight the fact that an action (wasting food) is done to the subject (food), often used when the actor is unknown or less important.
examples: N/A
N/A

grammarPoints.title: It **is important for us to understand** this problem.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: It is ... （for + （人ひとなど）） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: forを使つかうと、「（人ひとなど）が」「（人ひとなど）にとって」という意味いみが加くわわる。（不定詞ふていし）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This 'It is...' structure uses the infinitive phrase to understand as the real subject, and the addition of for us clarifies who the action is important for, meaning 'For us, doing this thing is important'.
examples: It **is necessary for everyone to care** about animals.
It’s **hard for us to solve** the problem.

grammarPoints.title: I **want everyone to know** about this problem.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: want + （人ひとなど） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: 「（人ひとなど）が…する ことを望のぞむ」「（人ひとなど）に …してほしい」という意味いみになる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure means 'to wish for (a person or thing) to do...' or 'to want (a person) to do...'.
examples: Riko **wants her classmates to read** their article.
Riko and Eddy **want** Mr. Tani **to review** their article.

grammarPoints.title: **Let** us **tell** you about sea otters. People **helped** sea otters **live** safely.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 使役動詞しえきどうし（let, help）: 〈let + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）に…させる」、 〈help + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）が…するのを助たすける」という意味いみになる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: These are causative verbs (let, help), followed by a person (object) and the plain form of the verb (infinitive without 'to'). Let means 'to allow/cause someone to do something,' and help means 'to assist someone in doing something'.
examples: Riko’s brother **helped her find** pictures for the newspaper.
**Let** Riko's brother **help** her.

grammarPoints.title: This graph **shows** the **increase** in the number of crested ibises.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: Real Life English (Graphs/Charts): グラフや表ひょうの活かつ用よう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Used for describing and interpreting visual data, typically employing verbs like shows or indicates, often combined with nouns like increase.
examples: N/A
N/A

grammarPoints.title: I **know where** the local shelter **is**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞し: 疑ぎ問もん詞しに主しゅ語ごと動どう詞しが続つづく形かたちで、名めい詞しのかたまりの働はたらきをする。（間接かんせつ疑ぎ問もん）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure uses an indirect question, where the question word is followed by a Subject-Verb order, and the entire clause functions as a noun (the object of the main verb know).
examples: Do you **know where** your homeroom teacher **lives**?
Do you **know where** the emergency exit **is**?

grammarPoints.title: **Tell** me **what** you **have done**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 動どう詞し + （人ひと） + whatなどで始はじまる節せつ: 「（人ひとに）（whatなどで始はじまる節せつの内ない容よう）を…する」という意味いみになる。（SVOO）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is an SVOO structure where the second object is an indirect question. It means 'to tell/inform someone about the content of the question'.
examples: Please **tell** me **what** we **should do** in a fire.
Please **teach** me **what** I **have to do**.

grammarPoints.title: There **is** a movie **called** Live Your Dream.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ分ぶん詞し: 過か去こ分ぶん詞しは、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…される［された］（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The Past Participle (called) is placed immediately after the noun (movie) to modify it, providing additional information that the movie 'is called' or 'has been named' this title.
examples: The movie **made** by an American director **moved** people both in Japan and the U.S.
The student exchange programs **held** every year **influence** a lot of students.

grammarPoints.title: The woman **smiling** in a kimono **is** Taylor.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し（...ing形けい）は、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…している（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The Present Participle (-ing form) placed after the noun (woman) modifies the noun, indicating that she is performing the action ('is smiling').
examples: The children **standing** behind the shelves **are** the students in Ishinomaki.
The girl **reading** a book **is** Riko.

grammarPoints.title: **Would you like me to carry** your umbrella?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: Real Life English (Helping in town): Would you like me to ～？（申もうし出でる）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: A polite way to offer assistance by asking if the listener desires the speaker to perform an action.
examples: N/A
N/A

grammarPoints.title: This **is** a picture **I found** on the internet.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 名めい詞しを修しゅう飾しょくする文ぶん: 「主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し＋目もく的てき語ご（名めい詞し）」の語ご順じゅんを入いれかえて、「名めい詞し＋主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し」とすると、前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして詳くわしい情じょう報ほうを加くわえることができる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is a noun phrase followed by a clause where the object relative pronoun (that/which) is omitted. This clause functions as post-modification, providing detail about the noun (picture).
examples: This is a picture **my uncle took**.
This **is** a picture **my father took**.

grammarPoints.title: Gandhi **is** a man **who has influenced** a lot of people.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 関かん係けい代だい名めい詞し who: 人ひとについて説せつ明めいを加くわえるときは、関かん係けい代だい名めい詞しのwhoを使つかう。（主しゅ格かく）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The relative pronoun who introduces a dependent clause that describes a person (a man), functioning as the subject of the clause.
examples: Jun **is** a boy **who loves** to play soccer.
Ms. Chen **is** a teacher **who came** from Canada two years ago.

grammarPoints.title: This **is** a movie **that** [which] **makes** people happy.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 関かん係けい代だい名めい詞し that [which]（主しゅ格かく）: ものについて説せつ明めいを加くわえるときは、関かん係けい代だい名めい詞しのthatまたはwhichを使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The relative pronoun that or which introduces a clause describing a thing (a movie) and functions as the subject of that clause.
examples: This is a T-shirt **that** [which] the students **designed** for Sports Day.
This is a book **that** [which] **is loved** by many people.

grammarPoints.title: This **is** a picture **that** [which] **I found** on the internet.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 関かん係けい代だい名めい詞し that [which]（目もく的てき格かく）: p.62 Key Sentences 15の文ぶんでは、thatまたはwhichを入いれることもできる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The relative pronoun that or which introduces a clause describing a thing (a picture) and functions as the object of the verb within that clause. In the objective case, the pronoun is often omitted.
examples: This is a picture **that** [which] **my father took**.
This is the book **that** [which] **I bought** yesterday.

grammarPoints.title: I do not **think** we **need** such a law.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: Real Life English (Opinion Article): I think that .... / I do not think that .... （意い見けんを述のべる）
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Used to express personal opinions or beliefs, especially in negation.
examples: N/A
N/A

grammarPoints.title: I **wish I could go** to school. I **wish I had** pens and notebooks.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 仮か定てい法ほう（I wish ...): 「…であればいいのに」と現げん実じつとは異ことなる願がん望ぼうを表あらわす。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Uses the I wish structure followed by a verb in the past tense (or could + base verb) to express a wish or desire that is contrary to the current reality.
examples: I **wish I had** more time to play.
I **wish there were** clean water to drink.

grammarPoints.title: If I **were** you, I **would ask** my friends for help.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 仮か定てい法ほう（If + 主しゅ語ご + were ...): 「…であれば～だろう（に）」と現げん実じつと異ことなることを仮か定ていして言いうときは〈If + 主しゅ語ご + be動どう詞しの過か去こ形けい（were）〉を使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This is the Conditional Mood (Hypothetical/Counterfactual) for non-real situations in the present. It uses the past form (were) in the if-clause and the conditional modal (would/could) in the main clause.
examples: If I **were** rich, I **could donate** a lot of money.
If I **were** a doctor, I **would save** many lives.

grammarPoints.title: If I **had** a school backpack, I **would donate** it.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 仮か定てい法ほう（If + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞しの過か去こ形けい, ....): if節せつ内ないで一い般ぱん動どう詞しや助じょ動どう詞しが使つかわれる場ば合あいも過か去こ形けいに なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Similar to KS 20, but uses the past tense of ordinary verbs (had) in the if-clause for hypothetical situations, followed by a conditional modal in the main clause.
examples: If I **went** there, I **would see** her.
If I **knew** her address, I **would send** her a letter.

grammarPoints.title: Many things **that** we see every day **come** from overseas.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 主しゅ語ごを説せつ明めいする関かん係けい代だい名めい詞し: 主しゅ語ごに説せつ明めいを加くわえる場ば合あい、主しゅ語ごと動どう詞しの間あいだに関かん係けい代だい名めい詞しの節せつが入はいり込こむ形かたちになる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: A relative clause (that we see every day) interrupts the main clause to modify the subject (Many things).
examples: The park **that I often visited has changed**.
The girl **who** came to our house before **is** Jun's friend.

grammarPoints.title: Tomorrow, on December 1, they **are going to attend** a summit meeting.

grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Uses the be going to future structure to describe a scheduled or planned event, often used in news reports.

exercises.translation: 彼女は来年留学する予定です。

exerciseSets.title: I **have been reading** a book **since** 4 p.m.
exerciseSets.topic: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう進しん行こう形けい

grammarPoint.title: I **have been reading** a book **since** 4 p.m.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう進しん行こう形けい: 〈have [has] + been + ...ing〉の形かたちで、過か去このある時ときから現げん在ざいまで、ある動どう作さが続つづいていることを表あらわす。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This is the Present Perfect Progressive Tense, using the structure ⟨have [has] + been + -ing⟩. It describes an action that started in the past and has been continuously ongoing until the present moment.
examples: Mr. Tani **has been checking** his students’ homework **since 4 p.m**.
It **has been raining** **for two days**.

exercises.question: I / have / been / reading / a / book / since / 4 / p.m.
exercises.answer: I have been reading a book since 4 p.m.
exercises.hint: 現げん在ざい完かん了りょう進しん行こう形けい: 〈have [has] + been + ...ing〉の形かたちで、過か去このある時ときから現げん在ざいまで、ある動どう作さが続つづいていることを表あらわす。
exercises.translation: 私は午後4時からずっと本を読んでいます。

exercises.question: I have ___ ___ for two hours.
exercises.answer: been studying
exercises.hint: have + been + -ing
exercises.translation: 私は2時間ずっと勉強しています。

exercises.question: It / has / been / raining / since / morning.
exercises.answer: It has been raining since morning.
exercises.hint: It + has + been + raining + since + morning.
exercises.translation: 朝からずっと雨が降っています。

exercises.question: She / has / been / playing / the / piano / for / two / hours.
exercises.answer: She has been playing the piano for two hours.
exercises.hint: She + has + been + playing + the + piano + for + two + hours.
exercises.translation: 彼女は2時間ずっとピアノを弾いています。

exercises.question: We / have / been / waiting / for / you.
exercises.answer: We have been waiting for you.
exercises.hint: We + have + been + waiting + for + you.
exercises.translation: 私たちはあなたをずっと待っていました。

exercises.question: They / have / been / talking / about / the / game.
exercises.answer: They have been talking about the game.
exercises.hint: They + have + been + talking + about + the + game.
exercises.translation: 彼らはその試合についてずっと話しています。

exerciseSets.title: It **is important for us to understand** this problem.
exerciseSets.topic: It is ... （for + （人ひとなど）） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい

grammarPoint.title: It **is important for us to understand** this problem.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: It is ... （for + （人ひとなど）） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: forを使つかうと、「（人ひとなど）が」「（人ひとなど）にとって」という意味いみが加くわわる。（不定詞ふていし）
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This 'It is...' structure uses the infinitive phrase to understand as the real subject, and the addition of for us clarifies who the action is important for, meaning 'For us, doing this thing is important'.
examples: It **is necessary for everyone to care** about animals.
It’s **hard for us to solve** the problem.

exercises.question: It / is / important / for / us / to / understand / this / problem.
exercises.answer: It is important for us to understand this problem.
exercises.hint: It is ... （for + （人ひとなど）） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: forを使つかうと、「（人ひとなど）が」「（人ひとなど）にとって」という意味いみが加くわわる。（不定詞ふていし）
exercises.translation: 私たちがこの問題を理解することは重要です。

exercises.question: It / is / important / for / me / to / study.
exercises.answer: It is important for me to study.
exercises.hint: It + is + important + for + me + to + study.
exercises.translation: 私が勉強することは重要です。

exercises.question: It is difficult ___ me ___ wake up early.
exercises.answer: for to
exercises.hint: Two prepositions needed.
exercises.translation: 私が早起きするのは難しいです。

exercises.question: It / is / necessary / for / you / to / read / books.
exercises.answer: It is necessary for you to read books.
exercises.hint: It + is + necessary + for + you + to + read + books.
exercises.translation: あなたが本を読むことは必要です。

exercises.question: It / is / easy / for / him / to / swim.
exercises.answer: It is easy for him to swim.
exercises.hint: It + is + easy + for + him + to + swim.
exercises.translation: 彼が泳ぐのは簡単です。

exercises.question: It / is / fun / for / them / to / play / soccer.
exercises.answer: It is fun for them to play soccer.
exercises.hint: It + is + fun + for + them + to + play + soccer.
exercises.translation: 彼らがサッカーをするのは楽しいです。

exerciseSets.title: I **want everyone to know** about this problem.
exerciseSets.topic: want + （人ひとなど） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい

grammarPoint.title: I **want everyone to know** about this problem.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: want + （人ひとなど） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: 「（人ひとなど）が…する ことを望のぞむ」「（人ひとなど）に …してほしい」という意味いみになる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This structure means 'to wish for (a person or thing) to do...' or 'to want (a person) to do...'.
examples: Riko **wants her classmates to read** their article.
Riko and Eddy **want** Mr. Tani **to review** their article.

exercises.question: I / want / everyone / to / know / about / this / problem.
exercises.answer: I want everyone to know about this problem.
exercises.hint: want + （人ひとなど） + to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい: 「（人ひとなど）が…する ことを望のぞむ」「（人ひとなど）に …してほしい」という意味いみになる。
exercises.translation: 私はみんなにこの問題について知ってほしいです。

exercises.question: I / want / you / to / clean / your / room.

exercises.translation: 私はあなたに部屋を掃除してほしいです。

exercises.question: I want you ___ be happy.
exercises.answer: to
exercises.hint: Infinitive marker.
exercises.translation: 私はあなたに幸せになってほしいです。

exercises.question: She / wants / me / to / help / her.
exercises.answer: She wants me to help her.
exercises.hint: She + wants + me + to + help + her.
exercises.translation: 彼女は私に手伝ってほしいと思っています。

exercises.question: My / mother / wants / me / to / be / a / doctor.
exercises.answer: My mother wants me to be a doctor.
exercises.hint: My + mother + wants + me + to + be + a + doctor.
exercises.translation: 母は私に医者になってほしいと思っています。

exercises.question: Do / you / want / me / to / help / you?
exercises.answer: Do you want me to help you?
exercises.hint: Do + you + want + me + to + help + you?
exercises.translation: 私に手伝ってほしいですか。

exerciseSets.title: **Let** us **tell** you about sea otters. People **helped** sea otters **live** safely.
exerciseSets.topic: 使役動詞しえきどうし（let, help）

grammarPoint.title: **Let** us **tell** you about sea otters. People **helped** sea otters **live** safely.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 使役動詞しえきどうし（let, help）: 〈let + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）に…させる」、 〈help + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）が…するのを助たすける」という意味いみになる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: These are causative verbs (let, help), followed by a person (object) and the plain form of the verb (infinitive without 'to'). Let means 'to allow/cause someone to do something,' and help means 'to assist someone in doing something'.
examples: Riko’s brother **helped her find** pictures for the newspaper.
**Let** Riko's brother **help** her.

exercises.question: Let / us / tell / you / about / sea / otters.
exercises.answer: Let us tell you about sea otters.
exercises.hint: 使役動詞しえきどうし（let, help）: 〈let + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）に…させる」、 〈help + （人ひとなど） + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉で 「（人ひとなど）が…するのを助たすける」という意味いみになる。
exercises.translation: ラッコについて話をさせてください。

exercises.question: People / helped / sea / otters / live / safely.
exercises.answer: People helped sea otters live safely.
exercises.hint: People + helped + sea + otters + live + safely.
exercises.translation: 人々はラッコが安全に暮らせるように助けました。

exercises.question: Let me ___ you.
exercises.answer: help
exercises.hint: Bare infinitive (no to).
exercises.translation: 手伝わせてください。

exercises.question: Let / me / introduce / myself.
exercises.answer: Let me introduce myself.
exercises.hint: Let + me + introduce + myself.
exercises.translation: 自己紹介をさせてください。

exercises.question: He / helped / me / carry / the / box.
exercises.answer: He helped me carry the box.
exercises.hint: He + helped + me + carry + the + box.
exercises.translation: 彼は私がその箱を運ぶのを手伝ってくれました。

exercises.question: Please / let / me / know / the / answer.
exercises.answer: Please let me know the answer.
exercises.hint: Please + let + me + know + the + answer.
exercises.translation: 答えを私に知らせてください。

exerciseSets.title: I **know where** the local shelter **is**.
exerciseSets.topic: 疑ぎ問もん詞し + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞し, 動どう詞し + （人ひと） + whatなどで始はじまる節せつ

grammarPoint.title: I **know where** the local shelter **is**.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞し: 疑ぎ問もん詞しに主しゅ語ごと動どう詞しが続つづく形かたちで、名めい詞しのかたまりの働はたらきをする。（間接かんせつ疑ぎ問もん）
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This structure uses an indirect question, where the question word is followed by a Subject-Verb order, and the entire clause functions as a noun (the object of the main verb know).
examples: Do you **know where** your homeroom teacher **lives**?
Do you **know where** the emergency exit **is**?

exercises.question: I / know / where / the / local / shelter / is.
exercises.answer: I know where the local shelter is.
exercises.hint: 疑ぎ問もん詞し + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞し: 疑ぎ問もん詞しに主しゅ語ごと動どう詞しが続つづく形かたちで、名めい詞しのかたまりの働はたらきをする。（間接かんせつ疑ぎ問もん）
exercises.translation: 私は地元の避難所がどこにあるか知っています。

exercises.question: I / know / where / the / library / is.
exercises.answer: I know where the library is.
exercises.hint: I + know + where + the + library + is.
exercises.translation: 私は図書館がどこにあるか知っています。

exercises.question: Do you know ___ ___ lives?
exercises.answer: where he
exercises.hint: Question word + subject + verb.
exercises.translation: あなたは彼がどこに住んでいるか知っていますか。

exercises.question: I / don't / know / who / he / is.
exercises.answer: I don't know who he is.
exercises.hint: I + don't + know + who + he + is.
exercises.translation: 私は彼が誰だか知りません。

exercises.question: Do / you / know / what / time / it / is?
exercises.answer: Do you know what time it is?
exercises.hint: Do + you + know + what + time + it + is?
exercises.translation: 今何時か知っていますか。

exercises.question: I / wonder / where / she / lives.
exercises.answer: I wonder where she lives.
exercises.hint: I + wonder + where + she + lives.
exercises.translation: 彼女はどこに住んでいるのかなあ。

exerciseSets.title: **Tell** me **what** you **have done**.
exerciseSets.topic: 疑ぎ問もん詞し + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞し, 動どう詞し + （人ひと） + whatなどで始はじまる節せつ

grammarPoint.title: **Tell** me **what** you **have done**.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 動どう詞し + （人ひと） + whatなどで始はじまる節せつ: 「（人ひとに）（whatなどで始はじまる節せつの内ない容よう）を…する」という意味いみになる。（SVOO）
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This is an SVOO structure where the second object is an indirect question. It means 'to tell/inform someone about the content of the question'.
examples: Please **tell** me **what** we **should do** in a fire.
Please **teach** me **what** I **have to do**.

exercises.question: Tell / me / what / you / have / done.
exercises.answer: Tell me what you have done.
exercises.hint: 動どう詞し + （人ひと） + whatなどで始はじまる節せつ: 「（人ひとに）（whatなどで始はじまる節せつの内ない容よう）を…する」という意味いみになる。（SVOO）
exercises.translation: あなたが何をしたか私に教えてください。

exercises.question: Tell / me / what / you / need.
exercises.answer: Tell me what you need.
exercises.hint: Tell + me + what + you + need.
exercises.translation: 何が必要か私に教えてください。

exercises.question: Show me ___ you made.
exercises.answer: what
exercises.hint: Question word for things.
exercises.translation: あなたが作ったものを私に見せてください。

exercises.question: Please / tell / me / where / you / live.
exercises.answer: Please tell me where you live.
exercises.hint: Please + tell + me + where + you + live.
exercises.translation: あなたがどこに住んでいるか教えてください。

exercises.question: He / asked / me / what / I / was / doing.
exercises.answer: He asked me what I was doing.
exercises.hint: He + asked + me + what + I + was + doing.
exercises.translation: 彼は私に何をしているのか尋ねました。

exercises.question: Can / you / tell / me / who / made / this / cake?
exercises.answer: Can you tell me who made this cake?
exercises.hint: Can + you + tell + me + who + made + this + cake?
exercises.translation: 誰がこのケーキを作ったか教えてくれますか。

exerciseSets.title: There **is** a movie **called** Live Your Dream.
exerciseSets.topic: 過か去こ分ぶん詞し, 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し

grammarPoint.title: There **is** a movie **called** Live Your Dream.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ分ぶん詞し: 過か去こ分ぶん詞しは、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…される［された］（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The Past Participle (called) is placed immediately after the noun (movie) to modify it, providing additional information that the movie 'is called' or 'has been named' this title.
examples: The movie **made** by an American director **moved** people both in Japan and the U.S.
The student exchange programs **held** every year **influence** a lot of students.

exercises.question: There / is / a / movie / called / Live / Your / Dream.
exercises.answer: There is a movie called Live Your Dream.
exercises.hint: 過か去こ分ぶん詞し: 過か去こ分ぶん詞しは、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…される［された］（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
exercises.translation: 『Live Your Dream』と呼ばれる映画があります。

exercises.question: This / is / a / book / written / by / Soseki.
exercises.answer: This is a book written by Soseki.
exercises.hint: This + is + a + book + written + by + Soseki.
exercises.translation: これは漱石によって書かれた本です。

exercises.question: The / language / spoken / in / Australia / is / English.
exercises.answer: The language spoken in Australia is English.
exercises.hint: The + language + spoken + in + Australia + is + English.
exercises.translation: オーストラリアで話されている言語は英語です。

exercises.question: I / have / a / bag / made / in / Italy.
exercises.answer: I have a bag made in Italy.
exercises.hint: I + have + a + bag + made + in + Italy.
exercises.translation: 私はイタリアで作られた鞄を持っています。

exercises.question: Do / you / know / the / boy / called / Tom?
exercises.answer: Do you know the boy called Tom?
exercises.hint: Do + you + know + the + boy + called + Tom?
exercises.translation: トムと呼ばれる少年を知っていますか。

exercises.question: Look / at / the / picture / painted / by / him.
exercises.answer: Look at the picture painted by him.
exercises.hint: Look + at + the + picture + painted + by + him.
exercises.translation: 彼によって描かれた絵を見てください。

exerciseSets.title: The woman **smiling** in a kimono **is** Taylor.
exerciseSets.topic: 過か去こ分ぶん詞し, 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し

grammarPoint.title: The woman **smiling** in a kimono **is** Taylor.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し（...ing形けい）は、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…している（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The Present Participle (-ing form) placed after the noun (woman) modifies the noun, indicating that she is performing the action ('is smiling').
examples: The children **standing** behind the shelves **are** the students in Ishinomaki.
The girl **reading** a book **is** Riko.

exercises.question: The / woman / smiling / in / a / kimono / is / Taylor.
exercises.answer: The woman smiling in a kimono is Taylor.
exercises.hint: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し: 現げん在ざい分ぶん詞し（...ing形けい）は、すぐ前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして、「…している（名めい詞し）」と情じょう報ほうを加くわえる。
exercises.translation: 着物を着て微笑んでいる女性はテイラーです。

exercises.question: The / girl / playing / tennis / is / my / sister.
exercises.answer: The girl playing tennis is my sister.
exercises.hint: The + girl + playing + tennis + is + my + sister.
exercises.translation: テニスをしている少女は私の妹です。

exercises.question: Look / at / the / bird / flying / in / the / sky.
exercises.answer: Look at the bird flying in the sky.
exercises.hint: Look + at + the + bird + flying + in + the + sky.
exercises.translation: 空を飛んでいる鳥を見てください。

exercises.question: Do / you / know / the / man / standing / over / there?
exercises.answer: Do you know the man standing over there?
exercises.hint: Do + you + know + the + man + standing + over + there?
exercises.translation: あそこに立っている男性を知っていますか。

exercises.question: I / received / a / letter / saying / he / was / fine.
exercises.answer: I received a letter saying he was fine.

exercises.translation: 彼が元気だという手紙を受け取りました。

exercises.question: Who / is / the / boy / running / in / the / park?
exercises.answer: Who is the boy running in the park?

exerciseSets.title: This **is** a picture **I found** on the internet.

grammarPoint.title: This **is** a picture **I found** on the internet.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 名めい詞しを修しゅう飾しょくする文ぶん: 「主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し＋目もく的てき語ご（名めい詞し）」の語ご順じゅんを入いれかえて、「名めい詞し＋主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し」とすると、前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして詳くわしい情じょう報ほうを加くわえることができる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This is a noun phrase followed by a clause where the object relative pronoun (that/which) is omitted. This clause functions as post-modification, providing detail about the noun (picture).
examples: This is a picture **my uncle took**.
This **is** a picture **my father took**.

exercises.question: This / is / a / picture / I / found / on / the / internet.
exercises.answer: This is a picture I found on the internet.
exercises.hint: 名めい詞しを修しゅう飾しょくする文ぶん: 「主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し＋目もく的てき語ご（名めい詞し）」の語ご順じゅんを入いれかえて、「名めい詞し＋主しゅ語ご＋動どう詞し」とすると、前まえの名めい詞しを後うしろから修しゅう飾しょくして詳くわしい情じょう報ほうを加くわえることができる。
exercises.translation: これは私がインターネットで見つけた写真です。

exercises.question: This / is / the / book / I / bought / yesterday.
exercises.answer: This is the book I bought yesterday.

exercises.translation: これは私が昨日買った本です。

exercises.question: The / movie / I / saw / last / night / was / interesting.

exercises.hint: The + movie + I + saw + last + night + was + interesting.
exercises.translation: 私が昨夜見た映画は面白かったです。

exercises.question: He / is / the / man / I / met / at / the / party.

exercises.translation: 彼は私がパーティーで会った男性です。

exercises.question: These / are / the / pictures / he / took / in / Kyoto.
exercises.answer: These are the pictures he took in Kyoto.
exercises.hint: These + are + the + pictures + he + took + in + Kyoto.
exercises.translation: これらは彼が京都で撮った写真です。

exercises.question: Is / this / the / CD / you / wanted?

exercises.translation: これはあなたが欲しかったCDですか。

exerciseSets.title: Gandhi **is** a man **who has influenced** a lot of people.

grammarPoint.title: Gandhi **is** a man **who has influenced** a lot of people.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 関かん係けい代だい名めい詞し who: 人ひとについて説せつ明めいを加くわえるときは、関かん係けい代だい名めい詞しのwhoを使つかう。（主しゅ格かく）
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The relative pronoun who introduces a dependent clause that describes a person (a man), functioning as the subject of the clause.
examples: Jun **is** a boy **who loves** to play soccer.

grammarPoint.title: I **wish I could go** to school. I **wish I had** pens and notebooks.

grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Uses the I wish structure followed by a verb in the past tense (or could + base verb) to express a wish or desire that is contrary to the current reality.
examples: I **wish I had** more time to play.
I **wish there were** clean water to drink.

exerciseSets.title: If I **were** you, I **would ask** my friends for help.
exerciseSets.topic: 仮か定てい法ほう（I wish ...), 仮か定てい法ほう（If + 主しゅ語ご + were ...)

grammarPoint.title: If I **were** you, I **would ask** my friends for help.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 仮か定てい法ほう（If + 主しゅ語ご + were ...): 「…であれば～だろう（に）」と現げん実じつと異ことなることを仮か定ていして言いうときは〈If + 主しゅ語ご + be動どう詞しの過か去こ形けい（were）〉を使つかう。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This is the Conditional Mood (Hypothetical/Counterfactual) for non-real situations in the present. It uses the past form (were) in the if-clause and the conditional modal (would/could) in the main clause.
examples: If I **were** rich, I **could donate** a lot of money.
If I **were** a doctor, I **would save** many lives.

grammarPoint.title: If I **had** a school backpack, I **would donate** it.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 仮か定てい法ほう（If + 主しゅ語ご + 動どう詞しの過か去こ形けい, ....): if節せつ内ないで一い般ぱん動どう詞しや助じょ動どう詞しが使つかわれる場ば合あいも過か去こ形けいに なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Similar to KS 20, but uses the past tense of ordinary verbs (had) in the if-clause for hypothetical situations, followed by a conditional modal in the main clause.
examples: If I **went** there, I **would see** her.
If I **knew** her address, I **would send** her a letter.

grammarPoint.title: Many things **that** we see every day **come** from overseas.
